wrong_text: cholera outbreak that killed over 10,000 people
problem: The official WHO/CDC death toll for the 2010-2019 Haiti cholera outbreak is approximately 9,606–9,789 — consistently reported as 'nearly 10,000', not 'over 10,000'. The threshold of 10,000 was never confirmed in official counts. Sources: WHO 2018 epidemiological report (9,606); CDC MMWR; Wikipedia 2010s Haiti cholera outbreak.
correction: cholera outbreak that killed nearly 10,000 people

wrong_text: Diarrhoeal disease kills around 485,000 people a year globally
problem: The 485,000 figure refers to child deaths (under ~9 years), not global all-age deaths. The WHO fact sheet (updated March 2024) states ~494,683 deaths per year in children under 9. Total all-age diarrhoeal deaths are approximately 1.17 million per year (IHME 2021). The lesson presents this as a global all-age total, which significantly understates the true burden. The figure also needs updating from 485,000 to ~495,000 for children. Correction: either specify 'children' or use the all-age figure. Source: WHO Diarrhoeal Disease fact sheet, March 2024; Our World in Data.
correction: Diarrhoeal disease kills around 1.5 million people a year globally, including around 495,000 children under the age of nine

wrong_text: sends it 1,432 km north by gravity canal to Beijing and Tianjin
problem: The Central Route is approximately 1,264–1,267 km long, not 1,432 km. Multiple authoritative sources give ~1,264km (Wikipedia) and ~1,267km (Coolgeography). The 1,432 km figure is not supported by any reliable source and is a significant overstatement of ~13%. Source: Wikipedia South-North Water Transfer Project; Coolgeography GCSE SNWTP.
correction: sends it around 1,267 km north by gravity canal to Beijing and Tianjin

wrong_text: Beijing now receives around 70% of its daily drinking water via this route
problem: The ~70% figure applies to the entire South-North Water Transfer Project (both Eastern and Central routes combined), not to the Central Route alone. Multiple sources confirm that the Central Route provides approximately 30% of Beijing's annual water consumption, while the total SNWTP (east + central) accounts for ~70-80% of Beijing's urban water supply. Attributing 70% specifically to the Central Route is factually incorrect. Sources: engineering.org.cn; SNWTP 5-years-on press release; sustainability-times.com.
correction: Beijing now receives around 70% of its daily drinking water via the project as a whole, with the Central Route being its primary source

problem: The most widely cited displacement figure for the Danjiangkou Reservoir expansion (Central Route) is approximately 330,000 people. Wikipedia gives 'around 330,000'; Coolgeography gives '300,000–330,000'; tutor2u gives '300,000'. The lesson's figure of 345,000 is at the high end of estimates and is not corroborated by mainstream GCSE or academic sources. The safe figure to use is 'around 330,000'. Source: Wikipedia South-North Water Transfer Project; Coolgeography; tutor2u AQA Geography reference.

wrong_text: Groundwater levels in the area rose by an average of around 4–5 metres within a few years of the johads' restoration
problem: The standard AQA GCSE figure for the Wakel/Wakal groundwater rise is 'up to 6 metres', as stated on tutor2u's AQA Geography reference (the primary GCSE revision resource for this case study). The lesson's 4–5 m understates the result and would give students the wrong number in the exam. Source: tutor2u AQA Geography Wakel River Basin case study ('raising the water table by up to 6m').
correction: Groundwater levels in the area rose by up to 6 metres within a few years of the johads' restoration

wrong_text: supplied drinking water to more than 140 million people
problem: By 2023 the project had already benefited well over 140 million people — multiple 2024 sources put the figure at 185 million+. The People's Daily 140-million figure dates from a 2021 report marking the 7-year anniversary of the Eastern Route. Stating '140 million' as the 2023 figure is a significant undercount. The lesson should use the more current figure. Source: China government official report Dec 2024 (185 million+); MDPI Water 2025 review.
correction: supplied drinking water to more than 185 million people
